To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the low temperature thermal conductivity κ of the honeycomb Kitaevin Heisenberg magnet α-RuCl3 increases by one order of magnitude when the magnetic field is increased above Bc≈7.6 T, and that this is due to a strong spin-phonon scattering in combination with a field-induced spin gap that reaches a value as large as ℏω0/kB=50 K at 20 T. The

(i) the low-temperature heat conduction of α-RuCL3 is strongly suppressed by spin-phonon scattering, which is enhanced by the Kitaev- Heisenberg excitations, and (ii) these excitations open a field-induced spin gap, which is large and linearly increases with the magnetic field.
the heat conductivity κ of the Kitaev-quantum-spin-liquid candidate α-RuCl3 increases by more than one order of magnitude beyond a magnetic field B_{c} of 7.5 T.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the magnetic properties and the heat transport of α-RuCL3.
the study of the magnetic properties of the Kitaev- Heisenberg honeycomb material α-RuCl3.
the investigation of the low-temperature properties of a new family of compounds, the so-called honeycomb iridates, which are based on the honeycomb structure of graphene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
α-RuCl3 is a quantum spin liquid, but not a Kitaev spin liquid.
the heat transport is strongly influenced by the spin-phonon interaction.

the magnetic field dependence of the low-temperature thermal conductivity in α-RuCL3 is a consequence of a field-induced energy gap in the magnetic excitation spectra and the associated strong scattering of phonons by magnetic excitations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found an unusual phonon heat transport in α-Rucl_{3}, which is caused by the spin-phonon scattering.

the heat conduction in α-Ru Cl_{3} is governed by a strong spin-phonon scattering in the low field phase, and the heat conduction is enhanced by the field-induced spin gap in the high field phase, which leads to a large increase of the heat conductivity.
we have shown that the magnetic field induced a spin gap in the magnetic excitation of α-Ru Cl3, and the phonon scattering is strongly suppressed in this spin-gapped phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heat transport can be a powerful probe to investigate quantum spin liquids and their excitations.

the heat conductivity of the Kitaev-quantum spin liquid α-RuCl3 is strongly affected by the magnetic field, which is a consequence of strong spin-phonon scattering and a magnetic field-induced spin gap.
the heat transport of a quantum spin-liquid candidate can be used as a sensitive probe of its magnetic excitation spectrum.
